turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. turn_history.text: It seems like you may be confusing alternate angles with angles that are equal. Let's focus on the definition of alternate angles in relation to the positions of angles \( p \) and \( q \) in the diagram. Can you think about how the positions of these angles relate to each other based on what we know about alternate angles?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, so alternate angles are on opposite sides of the line that crosses through, right? But I'm confused because you're saying they're not always equal... does that mean they're only equal sometimes? Like, when do they become equal?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with recognizing that alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal. They are equal only when the two intersected lines are parallel. Can you think about how the relationship between the intersected lines affects the equality of alternate angles?
